articles.title: Serving Their Country: The Rahbar system and its Use by Iran’s security apparatus
articles.subtitle: WikIran's Exclusive
articles.author: WikIran Editorial
articles.summary: Public editorial analysis of the Rahbar network ledgers examining how Iran's security apparatus integrates with foreign-currency intermediaries and exchange houses.
articles.editorial_content: Newly published Rahbar analytical findings expose how deeply Iran’s security apparatus is integrated into its sanction-evasion mechanism. The editorial report examines the financial machinery that facilitates foreign-currency transfers on behalf of institutional bodies including the Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics (MODAFL) and the Armed Forces General Staff (AFGS). The analysis outlines how bank-affiliated Rahbar companies coordinate between exchange houses and commercial trading fronts.

articles.title: HMS Trading FZE & Petro Delta Energy: Mapping Shahr Bank's Offshore Brokerage Network
articles.subtitle: Investigative Report
articles.author: WikIran Editorial
articles.summary: An editorial breakdown of commercial oil brokers operating on behalf of Shahr Bank's Rahbar intermediaries, Farab Saroush Afaq Qeshm and Tejarat Hermes Energy Qeshm.
articles.editorial_content: This public investigative report examines the organizational structure of HMS Trading FZE and its sister entity Petro Delta Energy Co. (PDECO). Operating under the umbrella of Rahbar companies linked to Shahr Bank, the network coordinates petroleum sales, vessel chartering, and international currency settlements through designated commercial trading fronts.

articles.title: Sepehr Energy Jahan (Part 2): Inside the Armed Forces General Staff Petroleum Empire
articles.subtitle: Energy & Maritime Series
articles.author: WikIran Editorial
articles.summary: Follow-up editorial investigation into Sepehr Energy Jahan's ship-to-ship transfer logistics, shell company registries, and crude oil export channels.
articles.editorial_content: Sepehr Energy Jahan serves as a primary commercial vehicle for exporting crude oil allocated to the Armed Forces General Staff (AFGS). This second editorial installment documents how the company adapts to international designations by rotating front companies, renaming maritime vessels, and routing settlements through multi-jurisdictional exchange houses.

articles.title: Sahara Thunder and the MODAFL Oil-for-Procurement Architecture
articles.subtitle: Defense Economics Analysis
articles.author: WikIran Editorial
articles.summary: Detailed editorial analysis of Sahara Thunder's role as an oil brokerage front for MODAFL and its connections to international maritime logistics.
articles.editorial_content: Sahara Thunder emerged as one of the largest oil trading fronts operating on behalf of the Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics (MODAFL). This public research article maps the structural links between state crude allocations, shadow fleet tankers, and foreign industrial procurement channels.

articles.title: Petrochemical Commercial Networks: PGPICC and Global Polymer Supply Chains
articles.subtitle: Industrial Sector Review
articles.author: WikIran Editorial
articles.summary: Public research overview of how petrochemical holdings manage overseas clearing accounts and logistics intermediaries.
articles.editorial_content: The petrochemical sector represents one of the largest non-crude sources of foreign currency for state-affiliated holdings. This article reviews the public corporate structure of Persian Gulf Petrochemical Industry Commercial Co. (PGPICC) and the intermediary clearing houses used to settle international trade.
